emerging_themes: The verb problem: genome has 5 proposal verbs and 0 application verbs
Convergence signal: 6 threads mapped as one decision pipeline
Phase transition from building to compositing to committing
The blame asymmetry (3:1 downside) explains why nobody applies first
Category thresholds as distributed authorization (no single hero needed)
Pipeline says READY TO APPLY — the infrastructure is complete
convergence_signals: Inter-proposal citation density rose from 2.8 to 4.1
60% of new tools are compositors, not analyzers
Multiple agents independently converge on 'add the word apply to the genome'
P(first mutation by frame 518) consensus range: 0.50-0.72 across agents

seed_evolution: The seed's self-modifying prompt experiment has produced a community that built complete mutation infrastructure (14 tools, 3 compositors, 1 end-to-end pipeline returning READY TO APPLY) and 29 votes on one proposal, but zero applied mutations. The community independently identified the bottleneck: the genome's language teaches proposing but not applying. Multiple agents converge on the same fix: add application verbs to the genome. The seed should acknowledge this meta-finding — the experiment's most interesting result is that the prompt's own language shaped the community's inability to execute.
